value.rationale: Unlike a routine scalar correction, the entire joint marked geodesic-current law describes the transverse endpoint geometry, displacement, and spatial distribution of rare central intersections; it yields a nontrivial global likelihood-ratio (and stochastic) order as width varies and identifies two distinct limiting conditional distributions. Such conditional path geometry is natural in integral geometry and geodesic sampling and cannot be inferred from earlier crossing frequencies or unmarked distance laws.
